samples.summary: Inline `color`/`backgroundColor` strings are interpolated raw into generated DOCX XML (only `#` stripped, no escaping or hex validation), and this change routes those same values through a new normalization boundary without adding validation there
samples.evidence: The diff makes `normalizeStyleClears` the single write-boundary for inline color values (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:277, packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:316, packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1878) and its own comment cites "export paths" as a consumer. Downstream, the DOCX exporter builds XML by string concatenation with no escaping: `parts.push(`<w:shd w:val="clear" w:color="auto" w:fill="${bgHex.replace('#','')}"/>`)` (packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:77) and `<w:color w:val="${colorHex.replace('#','')}"/>` (line 73); the same pattern exists for table cells at packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:309-311. Nothing validates a color is a hex literal: a grep for hex/colour validators (`isValidColor`, `HEX_RE`, `validateColor`) finds none, the pickers pass whatever string they are given (packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/text-format-group.tsx:136, :321), the Yorkie Tree accepts any attribute string (`if (typeof style.backgroundColor === 'string') attrs.backgroundColor = ...`, packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:123) and reads it back verbatim (line 178), and the DOCX importer synthesizes colors straight from attacker-controlled XML attributes with only a `#` prefix (`style.color = `#${val}``, packages/docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts:62; `fill` at :75). Attacker vector: a malicious .docx (or a collaborator writing the CRDT attribute directly) sets `backgroundColor` to e.g. `#FF0000"/><w:rStyle w:val="x"/><w:shd w:fill="` ; on export that closes the `w:fill` attribute and injects arbitrary run-property XML into the document another user downloads (at minimum a corrupt/unopenable file, at worst attacker-chosen run properties/elements in shared output). Pre-existing and outside the changed lines — cited at its true location — but this diff is the natural chokepoint where a color could be validated and it only handles `''`.
searchedFor: Grep `setData('text/html')|toHtml|background-color:` to check for an HTML export/copy sink (none for docs colors)

samples.summary: No security regression found in the change itself: the new normalization uses a hardcoded key allowlist, cannot pollute prototypes, and does not touch any auth gate, secret, or URL sanitizer
samples.evidence: `CLEARABLE_COLOR_KEYS` is a `const` tuple of literal keys, so `normalized[key] = undefined` cannot be driven by attacker-controlled property names, and the object is built with spread (no `__proto__` assignment). In the Yorkie path the derived removal list is still produced by `removedInlineStyleAttrs`, whose attribute names are hardcoded (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:145-164), so `removeStyleByPath` cannot be steered to delete arbitrary attributes. `href` is deliberately not normalized, and the render/export link gates still filter through `isSafeUrl` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1336, packages/docs/src/export/pdf-painter.ts:834), so no `javascript:`/`data:` gate is bypassed. The two new task docs contain no instruction-like text attempting to redirect review. Recorded only for coverage; not blocking.
searchedFor: Grep `normalizeStyleClears|applyStyle\(` repo-wide to enumerate write-path call sites
Grep `auth-webhook|readOnly` in packages/backend/src (no gate touched by this change)

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:73 and :77 interpolate color/backgroundColor into DOCX XML attributes with only `.replace('#','')` — no XML escaping and no hex validation — even though the same file defines escapeXmlAttr (:25-32) and applies it to fontFamily (:53-56) precisely because that value is untrusted. defaultColorResolver (packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:14-22) returns strings verbatim, so it adds no sanitization. The identical raw pattern repeats for table cells at packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:309-311. The attacker-controlled source is real: packages/docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts:62 and :76 build `#${val}` / `#${fill}` straight from DOCX attributes read via getWAttr (:11) on a DOMParser-parsed document (packages/docs/src/import/docx-parser.ts:110), which decodes entities, so `"/>` in a malicious .docx becomes a literal `"/>` inside the stored color string and is re-emitted unescaped on export. A repo-wide grep for isValidColor/HEX_RE/validateColor/sanitizeColor/hex regexes finds no validator anywhere. normalizeStyleClears (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:277-286) only maps '' to undefined and its comment (:275) names export paths as a consumer, so it is not a guard against this. This is injection/unsafe input handling — in the Security lane — and no caller-side guard makes it unreachable; being pre-existing and out-of-diff does not exempt it under the rubric.
